answer: An agent market allocating copper trellis contracts counts one allocation vote per credit permanently burned on its ledger, with no per-account bonus. A ripple of cloned accounts cannot multiply influence: each credit is spendable once, so a fixed balance buys the same total votes under any identity split. Extra influence requires acquiring more scarce, externally priced credits. Wealthy attackers can still buy control, and cheap credit issuance defeats the defense.
